paragraphs.sourceText: The start of high school doesn't have to be stressful
paragraphs.translationZh: 高中的开始不必有压力

paragraphs.sourceText: A) This month, more than 4 million students across the nation will begin high school. M皿y will do well. But many will not. Consider that nearly two-thirds of students will experience the "ninth-grade shock," which refers to a dramatic drop in a student's academic performance. Some students cope with this shock by avoiding challenges. For instance, they may drop difficult coursework. Others may experience a hopelessness that results in failing their core classes, such as English, science and math.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 本月，全国超过 400 万学生将开始高中生活。 M Glay 会做得很好。但很多人不会。考虑到近三分之二的学生会经历“九年级冲击”，这是指学生学业成绩的急剧下降。一些学生通过回避挑战来应对这种冲击。例如，他们可能会放弃困难的课程作业。其他人可能会感到绝望，导致核心课程（例如英语、科学和数学）不及格。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) This should matter a great deal to parents, teachers and policymakers. Ultimately it should matter to the students themselves and society at large, because students'experience of transitioning (过渡）to the ninth grade can have long.:term consequences not only for the students themselves but for their home communities. We m吐e these observations as research psychologists who have studied how schools and families can help young people thrive.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 这对于家长、教师和政策制定者来说应该非常重要。最终，这对学生本身和整个社会都很重要，因为学生过渡到九年级的经历不仅对学生本身而且对他们的家庭社区都会产生长期影响。我们作为研究心理学家发表了这些观察结果，他们研究了学校和家庭如何帮助年轻人成长。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) In the new global economy, students who fail to finish the ninth grade with passing grades in college preparatory coursework are very unlikely to graduate on time and ,go on to get jobs. One study has calculated that the lifetime benefit to the local economy for a single additional student who completes high school is half a m诅ion dollars or more. This is based on higher earnings and avoided costs in health care, crime, welfare dependence and other things.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 在新的全球经济中，未能通过大学预科课程完成九年级课程的学生不太可能按时毕业并继续找到工作。一项研究计算出，每多一名完成高中学业的学生，​​对当地经济的终生效益可达半百万美元或更多。这是基于更高的收入和避免的医疗保健、犯罪、福利依赖和其他方面的成本。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) The consequences of doing poorly in the ninth grade can impact more than students'ability to find a good job. It can also impact the extent to which they enjoy life. Students lose many of the friends they turned to for support when they move from the eighth to the ninth grade. One study of ninth-grade students found that 50 percent of friendships among ninth graders changed from one month to the next, signaling striking instability in friendships.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 九年级表现不佳的后果不仅仅影响学生找到好工作的能力。它还会影响他们享受生活的程度。当学生从八年级升到九年级时，他们失去了许多寻求支持的朋友。一项针对九年级学生的研究发现，九年级学生中 50% 的友谊从一个月到下个月都发生了变化，这表明友谊存在显着的不稳定。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) In addition, studies find the first year of high 妃hool typically shows one of the greatest increases in depression of any year over the lifespan. Researchers think that one explanation is that ties to friends are broken while academic demands are rising. Furthermore, most adult cases of clinical depression first emerge in adolescence (青春期）. The World Health Organization reports that depression has the greatest burden of disease worldwide, in terms of the total cost of treatment and the loss of productivity.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 此外，研究发现，高妃呼的第一年通常是一生中抑郁症增加最多的一年。研究人员认为，一种解释是，随着学业要求的提高，与朋友的联系被打破。此外，大多数成人临床抑郁症病例首先出现在青春期。世界卫生组织报告称，就治疗总成本和生产力损失而言，抑郁症是全世界最大的疾病负担。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Given all that's riding on having a successful ninth grade experience, it pays to explore what: can be done to meet the academic, social and emotional challenges of the transition to high school. So far, our studies have yielded one main insight: Students'beliefs about change-their beliefs about whether people are stuck one way forever, or whether people can change their personalities and abilities-are related to their ability to cope, succeed academically and maintain good mental health. Past research has called these beliefs " mindsets (思维模式），" with a "fixed mindset" referring to the belief that people cannot change and a "growth mindset" referring to the belief that people can change.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 考虑到这一切都依赖于成功的九年级经历，探索什么是值得的：可以采取哪些措施来应对向高中过渡的学业、社交和情感挑战。到目前为止，我们的研究得出了一个主要结论：学生对改变的信念——他们对人们是否会永远陷入一种困境的信念，或者人们是否可以改变他们的性格和能力的信念——与他们的应对能力、学业成功和保持良好的心理健康有关。过去的研究将这些信念称为“思维模式”，其中“固定心态”指的是人们无法改变的信念，“成长心态”指的是人们可以改变的信念。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) In one recent study, we examined 360 adolescents' beliefs about the nature of "smartness"—that is, their fixed mindsets about intelligence. We then assessed biological stress responses for students whose grades were dropping by examining their stress加rmones (荷尔蒙）. Students who believed that intelligence is fixed—that you are stuck being "not smart" if you struggle in school—showed higher levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining at the beginning of the ninth grade. If students believed that intelligence could improve-that is to say, when they held more of a growth mindset of intelligence-they showed lower levels of stress hormones when their grades were declining. This was an exciting result because it showed that the body's stress responses are not determined solely by one's grades. Instead, declining grades only predicted worse stress hormones among students who believed that worsening grades were a permanent and hopeless state of affairs.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 在最近的一项研究中，我们调查了 360 名青少年对“聪明”本质的信念，即他们对智力的固定心态。然后，我们通过检查成绩下降的学生的压力加蒙（荷尔蒙）来评估成绩下降的学生的生物压力反应。那些相信智力是固定的学生——如果你在学校表现不佳，你就会陷入“不聪明”的境地——在九年级开始时成绩下降时，他们会表现出较高水平的压力激素。如果学生相信智力可以提高，也就是说，当他们持有更多的智力成长心态时，他们在成绩下降时表现出较低水平的压力激素。这是一个令人兴奋的结果，因为它表明身体的压力反应不仅仅取决于一个人的成绩。相反，成绩下降只会预示着那些认为成绩下降是一种永久且无望的情况的学生的压力荷尔蒙会更差。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) We also investigated the social side of the high school transition. In this study, instead of teaching students that their smartness can change, we taught them that their social standing—that is, whether they are bullied or excluded or left out一can change over time. We then looked at high school students' stress responses to daily social difficulties. That is, we taught them a growth mindset about their social lives. In this study, students came into the laboratory and were asked to give a public speech in front of upper-year students. The topic of the speech was what makes one popular in high school. Following this, students had to complete a difficult mental math task in front of the same upper-year students.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 我们还调查了高中过渡的社会方面。在这项研究中，我们并没有告诉学生他们的聪明程度可以改变，而是告诉他们他们的社会地位——也就是说，他们是否被欺负、被排斥或被排除在外——可以随着时间的推移而改变。然后我们研究了高中生对日常社交困难的压力反应。也就是说，我们教给他们关于社交生活的成长心态。在这项研究中，学生们进入实验室，并被要求在高年级学生面前发表公开演讲。演讲的主题是一个人在高中受欢迎的原因。接下来，学生们必须在高年级学生面前完成一项困难的心算任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Experiment results showed that students who were not taught that people can change showed poor stress responses. When these students gave the speech, their blood vessels contracted and their hearts pumped less blood through the body-both responses that the body shows when it is preparing for damage or defeat after a physical threat. Then they gave worse speeches and made more mistakes in math. But when students were taught that people can change, they had better responses to stress, in part because they felt like they had the resources to deal with the demanding situation. Students who got the growth mindset intervention (干预）showed less-contracted blood vessels and their hearts pumped more blood—both of which contributed to more oxygen getting to the brain, and, ultimately, better performance on the speech and mental math tasks.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 实验结果表明，没有被教导人可以改变的学生表现出较差的压力反应。当这些学生发表演讲时，他们的血管收缩，心脏向身体泵出的血液减少——这两种反应都是身体在受到身体威胁后准备遭受伤害或失败时表现出来的。然后他们的演讲更糟糕，数学也犯了更多错误。但当学生们被告知人可以改变时，他们对压力有更好的反应，部分原因是他们觉得自己有资源来应对困难的情况。接受成长心态干预的学生表现出血管收缩较少，心脏泵出更多血液，这两者都有助于更多氧气进入大脑，最终在演讲和心算任务中表现更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) These findings lead to several possibilities that we are investigating further. First, we are working to replicate (复制）these findings in more diverse school communities. We want to know in which types of schools and for which kinds of students these growth mindset ideas help young people adapt to the challenges of high school. We also hope to learn how teachers, parents or school counselors can help students keep their ongoing academic or social difficulties in perspective. We wonder what would happen if schools helped to make beliefs about the potential for change and improvement a larger feature of the overall school culture, especially for students starting the ninth grade.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 这些发现引出了我们正在进一步调查的几种可能性。首先，我们正在努力在更多元化的学校社区中复制这些发现。我们想知道在哪些类型的学校和哪些类型的学生中，这些成长心态理念可以帮助年轻人适应高中的挑战。我们还希望了解教师、家长或学校辅导员如何帮助学生正确看待他们持续存在的学业或社会困难。我们想知道，如果学校帮助人们相信改变和改进的潜力成为整个学校文化的一个更大的特征，特别是对于九年级开始的学生来说，会发生什么。

paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 患有抑郁症的人数在高中第一年急剧增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: In fact many experts argue that the most important 21st-century skills aren't related to specific technologies or subject matter, but to creativity; skills like imagination, problem-finding and problem­ solving, teamwork, optimism, patience and the ability to experiment and talce risks. These are skills acquired when kids tinker (鼓捣小玩意）. High-tech industries such as NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory

paragraphs.sourceText: have found that their best overall problem solvers were master tinkerers in their youth.

paragraphs.sourceText: There are cognitive (认知的）benefits of doing things the way we did as children—building something, tearing it down, then building it up again. Research shows that given 15 minutes of free play, four- and five-year-olds will spend a third of this time engaged in spatial, mathematical, and architectural activities. This type of play—especially with building blocks一helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 以我们小时候的方式做事对认知有好处——建造一些东西，拆掉它，然后再建造它。研究表明，四五岁的孩子有 15 分钟的自由游戏时间，其中三分之一的时间会花在空间、数学和建筑活动上。这种类型的游戏——尤其是积木游戏——可以帮助孩子们发现和发展数学和几何的关键原理。

paragraphs.sourceText: If play and b叫ding are critical to 21st-century skill development, that's really good news for two reasons: Children are born builders, makers, and creators, so fostering (培养）21st-century skills may be as simple as giving kids room to play, tinker and try things out, even as they grow older. Secondly, it doesn't talce 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills. This is especially important for under­ resourced schools and communities. Talcing whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果玩耍和玩耍对 21 世纪的技能发展至关重要，那么这确实是个好消息，原因有二：儿童是天生的建设者、创造者和创造者，因此培养 21 世纪的技能可能很简单，只要给孩子们玩耍、修补和尝试的空间，即使他们长大了也是如此。其次，培养 21 世纪的技能并不需要 21 世纪的技术。这对于资源匮乏的学校和社区尤其重要。滑稽任何方便的材料并修补它们是一个

paragraphs.sourceText: Being an information technology, or IT, worker is not a job I envy. They are the ones who, right in the middle of a critical meeting, are expected to instantly fix the projector that's no longer working. They have to tolerate the bad tempers of colleagues frustrated at the number of times they've had to call the help desk for the same issue. They are also the ones who know there are systems that are more powerful, reliable and faster, but their employer simply will not put up the funds to buy them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为一名信息技术工作者并不是我羡慕的工作。他们是那些在关键会议进行中，需要立即修复不再工作的投影仪的人。他们不得不忍受同事的坏脾气，因为他们因同一问题多次致电服务台而感到沮丧。他们也知道有更强大、更可靠、更快的系统，但他们的雇主根本不会出钱购买这些系统。

paragraphs.sourceText: According to a recent survey, employees who have a job reliant on IT support consider IT a major source of job dissatisfaction. Through no fault of their own, they can suddenly find their productivity deteriorating or quality control non-existent. And there's little they can do about it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最近的一项调查显示，工作依赖 IT 支持的员工认为 IT 是工作满意度的主要来源。尽管并非他们自己的过错，他们可能会突然发现自己的生产力下降或质量控制不存在。他们对此无能为力。

paragraphs.sourceText: The experience of using IT penetrates almost the entire work field. It has become a crucial part of employees' overall work experience. When IT is operating as it should, employee self-confidence swells. Their job satisfaction, too, can surge when well-functioning machines relieve them of dull tasks or repetitive processes. But if there's one thing that triggers widespread employee frustration, it's an IT transformation project gone wrong, where swollen expectations have been popped and a long list of promised efficiencies have been reversed. This occurs when business leaders implement IT initiatives with little consideration of how those changes will impact the end user.
paragraphs.translationZh: 使用IT的体验几乎渗透到整个工作领域。它已成为员工整体工作体验的重要组成部分。当 IT 正常运行时，员工的自信心就会增强。当运转良好的机器将他们从枯燥的任务或重复的过程中解放出来时，他们的工作满意度也会大幅提高。但如果有一件事引发了员工普遍的挫败感，那就是 IT 转型项目出了问题，过高的期望落空了，一长串承诺的效率也被推翻了。当业务领导者实施 IT 计划时很少考虑这些变化将如何影响最终用户时，就会发生这种情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: Which is why managers should appreciate just how influential the IT user experience is to their employees, and exert substantial effort in ensuring their IT team eliminates programming errors and application crashes. Adequate and timely IT support should also be available to enable users to cope with technological issues at work. More importantly, IT practitioners need to understand what employees experience mentally when they use IT.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这就是为什么管理者应该认识到 IT 用户体验对其员工的影响有多大，并付出巨大努力来确保 IT 团队消除编程错误和应用程序崩溃。还应提供充足、及时的 IT 支持，使用户能够应对工作中的技术问题。更重要的是，IT从业者需要了解员工在使用IT时的心理体验。

paragraphs.sourceText: Therefore, businesses need to set up their IT infrastructure so that it is designed to fit in with their employees'work, rather than adjust their work to fit in with the company's IT limitations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，企业需要建立自己的 IT 基础设施，使其适合员工的工作，而不是调整员工的工作以适应公司的 IT 限制。
